messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: KV cache eviction rate spike + continuous-batch latency degradation detected in us-west-2. Auto-escalating to on-call. trace_id=cb-7f3a

maria_g: Ack. I'm on it. Seeing steady increase in batch assembly time and timeouts in the cont-batch worker logs. Initial suspicion: recent config change to max_num_seqs on the cont-batcher (deployed ~45m ago) may be causing oversized batching + paging pressure.

cheng_li: Can you share the deploy id / diff? I think the change lowered max_num_seqs from 512 -> 64 for latency reasons, but that can make max_batch_tokens blow up when many short seqs are present.

maria_g: Deploy id: deploy/infra-contbatch/2026-03-15-1123. Relevant diff: reduced max_num_seqs=512 -> 64, also tightened batch timeout from 80ms -> 12ms.

sarah_v: That combination would increase number of partial batches and cause more frequent KV cache evictions and paging. Customer-observed symptom: requests hitting timeout (HTTP 504) for long-context models.

incident-bot: Recent alerts: cont-batch-timeout > 5s (service: inference-gateway) x 1200 events in 10m, KV-cache-eviction-rate 8x baseline.

maria_g: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert max_num_seqs to 512 2) temporarily increase cont-batch timeout to 200ms 3) throttle incoming burst traffic for low-tier to reduce pressure. I'll run steps 1 and 2 and report back.

cheng_li: +1. Also set max_batch_tokens=8192 to avoid single-batch token explosion.

maria_g: Running rollback now.

maria_g: Command I ran:
```bash
# rollback cont-batch config to stable
kubectl set env deployment/cont-batcher -n infra CONTB_MAX_NUM_SEQS=512 CONTB_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=8192 CONTB_TIMEOUT_MS=200
# bump configmap with safe defaults
kubectl rollout restart deployment/cont-batcher -n infra
```

maria_g: Rolling restart initiated. Watching logs.

ryan_ops: Noted. I'm enabling a temporary ingress qps cap for free-tier customers to reduce noise: setting rate-limit 50r/s per org for 15m.

customer_escalations: Heads up — AcmeHealth and FinApps reported elevated tail latency and ~2-3% request failures in the last 20m. They may have open support tickets. Prioritizing contact with AcmeHealth (SLA).

cheng_li: Are we also seeing increased disk paging on GPU hosts? Could be evictions from KV cache writing to disk causing IO stall.

maria_g: Disk IO looks normal, but memory pressure on the cache nodes spiked. Eviction storm caused high GC churn. KV cache eviction traces attached in logs with tag cb-7f3a.

sarah_v: Can we temporarily disable prefix caching for the affected model family to reduce write amplification? That was effective in last similar incident.

maria_g: Doing that now for model-family /redwood-llama/13b.

maria_g: Command:
```bash
# disable prefix cache for family to stop aggressive writes
kubectl patch cm/kvcache-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"prefix_cache_enabled":"false"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/kvcache -n infra
```

maria_g: Observed metrics: within 90s eviction rate down ~70%, cont-batch assembly latency trending down. Overall API p50/p95 improving.

incident-bot: Auto-escalation cleared. Next check in 5m.

customer_escalations: AcmeHealth on call says errors dropped after ~6m, but they saw a retry storm from their client side — asking for root cause and compensation guidance.

ryan_ops: I've added a temporary alert mute on noisy low-tier orgs and adjusted the threshold for cont-batch-timeout from 1s -> 3s to avoid alert thrashing while we stabilize.

alex_p: Quick note for handoff: maria, could you summarize what we've changed and the real hit to customers so I can brief SEs?

maria_g: Summary for handoff -> Sarah (taking over):
- Root cause: aggressive cont-batch config changes (max_num_seqs lowered + timeout lowered) increased partial batches under bursty short-seq traffic, causing more frequent KV cache evictions and GC pressure -> increased tail latencies and some timeouts.
- Mitigations applied: rolled max_num_seqs -> 512, set max_batch_tokens=8192, increased cont-batch timeout to 200ms, disabled prefix cache for /redwood-llama/13b, throttled free-tier ingress.
- Customer impact: 2 enterprise customers (AcmeHealth, FinApps) reported elevated tail latency and ~2-3% increased request failures for ~25m window; failed requests mostly recovered after mitigations.
- Current status: systems stable, eviction rate back to baseline, cont-batch latency back within SLO. Monitoring for 1h.

sarah_v: Taking over on-call. Thanks @maria_g. I'll keep watch for the next hour and initiate postmortem once we confirm stability. Handoff notes copied to #eng-oncall.

sarah_v: Action items for postmortem / follow-up:
- Rollback policy: add canary gating for cont-batch config changes; require simulation on synthetic short-seq bursts.
- Alert tuning: add composite alert linking eviction_rate + cont-batch-timeout to reduce noisy pages.
- Customer follow-up: SEs to contact AcmeHealth + FinApps with timeline and mitigation; discuss credit if needed.
- Code/Config: enforce maximums for max_batch_tokens and decrease sensitivity of max_num_seqs to tiny values.

maria_g: I'll file the incident ticket and start collecting logs/traces, will include deploy id and config diff.

incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1159 (contbatch-config-induced-eviction-storm). Priority: P2.

customer_escalations: I'll draft customer messages and coordinate with SEs.

ryan_ops: Postmortem owner volunteers? I'll take remediation on alerting and throttling knobs.

maria_g: I'll own the runbook updates and the canary gating work.

sarah_v: Marking handoff complete. If nothing regresses in the next 60m, we'll move to postmortem phase. :thumbsup:

maria_g: Update @here: 35 minutes after mitigation metrics remain stable, eviction rate normal, API errors at baseline. Closing immediate incident channel and tracking actions in INC-2026-1159.

sarah_v: Closing the incident thread. Follow-ups will appear in the incident ticket. Thanks everyone for quick coordination. :heart:
